cards.name: split-the-schedule-per-n-k-not-the-kernel-quantized-gemm-gfx950-prefill
cards.description: One constexpr GEMM chassis with a per-(N,K) schedule table (tile order, XCD undo, waves-per-eu) beats every single global schedule on a two-shape fp8 seam.
cards.key: one Triton fp8 A8W8 block-scaled GEMM entry serving two very different N-widths in prefill on gfx950/CDNA4, replacing a tuned CK MPadding instance
cards.effect: 1.0491x weighted isolated (director-verified) over a TUNED vendor MPadding instance; per case the wide-N arm (N=34816, K=5120) is 1.065/1.079 at M=1109/588 against 1.041/1.058 for the best single global schedule, and the narrow-N arm (N=7168) is 1.125/1.104 against 1.057/1.011
cards.roofline: LDS-bound before (~43% of LDS accesses conflicted, ~21% of all kernel cycles) -> latency-bound, dependency-wait dominant after (wave cycles ~24% active / ~42% dependency wait / ~34% issue wait), MFMA ~27% busy at ~30% of dense fp8 peak
cards.title: Split the schedule per (N,K), not the kernel
cards.lever: when one entry serves two shapes whose N-tile counts differ by an order of magnitude, keep one binary and one tile and make the SCHEDULE a constexpr parameter set chosen per (N,K): traversal order, whether the XCD round-robin is undone, and waves-per-eu each flip sign between the arms.
cards.apply: constexpr order / num-xcds / waves-per-eu plus a clamped M tail (min(offs_m, M-1)) on both arms, selected from a small host table keyed on (N,K); here the wide-N arm took M-fastest + an 8-XCD round-robin undo and the narrow-N arm took N-fastest, no remap, waves-per-eu=2.
cards.stack:
total 1.0491x weighted isolated (director-verified) = one hand-integrated chassis merging three same-round directions, none of which wins alone
  - 1. LDS/weight-stream schedule lane - 1.0345x standalone (round 1, verified) - the chassis the merge was built on; it drove conflicted LDS accesses to zero, which converted ~22% of cycles into only ~5% of wall time
  - 2. clamped M tail + column-major order with the XCD round-robin undo - carried out of a direction verified 1.0408x standalone whose own persistent/balanced-grid premise lost 5-11%
  - 3. the narrow-N schedule (N-fastest, no remap, waves-per-eu=2) - carried out of a direction that verified 0.9974x, i.e. a LOSS on the graded metric
  - note: the three landed in one merge, so these are standalone-vs-frozen-baseline ratios, not incremental contributions; two further rounds added 0.
cards.verify: confirm each arm's schedule actually engaged by diffing AMDGCN across the table's configs compiled in one process, then take >=5-run interleaved medians per case against the frozen baseline on an idle box, with a no-op control measured the same way.
cards.pitfall:
a fan-out direction headlined a win and was a loss on the graded metric -> it reported an unweighted geomean while the metric of record is time-weighted, and the one case it lost carried ~47% of the weight -> score every candidate on the graded weighted metric and read its per-case lines.
a shape-scoped change moved the aggregate UP while regressing that shape ~21% on both its cases -> that shape is ~22% of the weight, so ordinary drift on the heavy shape covers it -> judge a shape-scoped change on that shape's own cases.
widening the loop body (a second accumulator, deeper pipeline stages) lost 12-52% with registers free -> the pipeliner allocates one LDS buffer set per load pair per stage, and the run's metrics JSON reported zero static LDS while the compiler reported 32 KB/CTA -> read shared bytes off the compiled kernel and price any widening in LDS first.
an 'underfilled, high cost-per-CTA' signal nominated a whole parallelism round -> it was a fixed weight-stream cost divided by a small CTA count; a graph-captured fill sweep showed 4x the CTAs at equal time and then a residency cliff at half the slot count previously assumed -> run that sweep before funding a fill/occupancy direction.
single-run screening flipped on a byte-identical repeat (1.109 then 1.054) -> ~1% harness noise over a no-op floor of median 1.013 / max 1.042 -> gate on medians, not single runs.
cards.caution: also verify which knob actually causes the counter you plan to attack: the VALU excess on the wide-N arm came entirely from waves-per-eu, while the tile order and the XCD remap changed the K-loop by zero instructions - a static opcode histogram across configs compiled in one process settles that where a ~1%-noise A/B cannot.
